q.t: Find sin 18°/cos 72°.
q.e: 18° and 72° add to 90°, so sin 18° = cos 72°.

q.t: Find cos 48° − sin 42°.
sin(90° − θ) equals…
q.e: In a right triangle the two acute angles are θ and 90° − θ; the side opposite one is adjacent to the other.

q.t: tan(90° − θ) equals…
q.e: Opposite and adjacent swap roles for the other acute angle, so opp/adj becomes adj/opp.

q.t: If sin A = cos 30° (A acute), find A in degrees.
Find cosec 31° − sec 59°.
q.e: sec 59° = cosec(90° − 59°) = cosec 31°.

q.t: Find tan 35° × tan 55°.
If tan A = cot B (A, B acute), find A + B in degrees.
q.e: cot B = tan(90° − B), so A = 90° − B.

q.t: sec 70° = cosec x°. Find x.
q.e: sec θ = cosec(90° − θ).

q.t: Write cot 85° + cos 75° using angles between 0° and 45°.
Find 2 sin 36°/cos 54° − sec 32°/cosec 58°.
q.e: sin 36° = cos 54° and sec 32° = cosec 58°, so 2 × 1 − 1.

q.t: If tan 3A = cot(A − 26°) with 3A acute, find A.
If sec 2A = cosec(A − 36°) with 2A acute, find A.
q.e: cosec(A − 36°) = sec(126° − A), so 2A = 126° − A and A = 42°.

q.t: Find sin 25° cos 65° + cos 25° sin 65°.
q.e: cos 65° = sin 25° and sin 65° = cos 25°, giving sin² 25° + cos² 25°.

q.t: Find tan 10° tan 20° tan 70° tan 80°.
q.e: Pair complements: tan 10° tan 80° = 1 and tan 20° tan 70° = 1.

q.t: A, B, C are the angles of a triangle. sin((B + C)/2) equals…
Find cos² 20° + cos² 70°.
q.e: cos 70° = sin 20°, so it is cos² 20° + sin² 20°.

q.t: Find sin(50° + θ) − cos(40° − θ).
q.e: (50° + θ) + (40° − θ) = 90°, so the sine of one equals the cosine of the other.

q.t: Find cosec 39° cos 51° + tan 21° cot 69° − sec² 21°.
q.e: cos 51° = sin 39°, so the first term is 1; cot 69° = tan 21°. That gives 1 + tan² 21° − sec² 21° = 0.

q.t: If sin 3θ = cos(θ − 6°) with 3θ and θ − 6° acute, find θ.
q.e: Complementary: 3θ + θ − 6° = 90°, so 4θ = 96°.

q.t: Find cos 70°/sin 20° + cos 59°/sin 31° − 2 sin² 45°.
q.e: Each fraction is 1 (complements), and 2 sin² 45° = 2 × 1/2 = 1: 1 + 1 − 1.

q.t: Find (tan 20°/cosec 70°)² + (cot 20°/sec 70°)² + 2 tan 15° tan 45° tan 75°.
q.e: cosec 70° = sec 20°, so the first is sin² 20°; likewise the second is cos² 20°. tan 15° tan 75° = 1. So 1 + 2.

q.t: Find tan 1° tan 2° tan 3° … tan 89°.
q.e: Pair tan θ with tan(90° − θ) = cot θ: every pair gives 1, and the middle term is tan 45° = 1.

q.t: Find cos 1° cos 2° cos 3° … cos 180°.
q.e: One of the factors is cos 90° = 0.

q.t: If cot θ = tan(2θ − 45°) with both angles acute, find θ.
q.e: cot θ = tan(90° − θ), so 2θ − 45° = 90° − θ and θ = 45°.

q.t: Find sin² 5° + sin² 10° + sin² 15° + … + sin² 85° + sin² 90°.
q.e: Pair sin² θ + sin²(90° − θ) = 1: 5° with 85° … 40° with 50° gives 8. Add sin² 45° = 1/2 and sin² 90° = 1.

q.t: Write sin 67° + cos 75° using angles between 0° and 45°.
If A + B = 90°, simplify √(tan A tan B + tan A cot B) ÷ (sin A sec B).
q.e: tan B = cot A, so tan A tan B = 1, and cot B = tan A. √(1 + tan² A) = sec A. And sec B = cosec A, so sin A sec B = 1.

q.t: Find cos 38° cos 52° − sin 38° sin 52°.
q.e: cos 52° = sin 38° and sin 52° = cos 38°, so the two terms are equal.

q.t: In ΔABC, tan((A + B)/2) equals…
q.e: (A + B)/2 = 90° − C/2, and tan(90° − x) = cot x.

q.t: Find cosec 25°/sec 65° + 3 tan 12° tan 33° tan 45° tan 57° tan 78° − 2(cos² 40° + cos² 50°).
q.e: First term 1; the tan product pairs to 1 × 1 × 1, so 3; cos² 40° + cos² 50° = 1, so −2. Total 2.

q.t: Find cos 58°/sin 32° + sin 22°/cos 68° − (cos 38° cosec 52°)/(tan 18° tan 35° tan 45° tan 72° tan 55°).
q.e: Each of the first two is 1. cos 38° cosec 52° = 1 and the tan product is 1, so the last fraction is 1.

q.t: If sec 5A = cosec(A + 30°) with 5A acute, find A.
q.e: sec 5A = cosec(90° − 5A), so 90° − 5A = A + 30° and A = 10°.

q.t: If sin(θ + 36°) = cos θ with both angles acute, find θ.
q.e: The angles are complementary: θ + 36° + θ = 90°.

q.t: Find (cos(90° − θ) sec(90° − θ) tan θ)/(cosec(90° − θ) sin(90° − θ) cot(90° − θ)) − tan(90° − θ)/cot θ.
q.e: The first fraction is (sin θ cosec θ tan θ)/(sec θ cos θ tan θ) = 1; the second is cot θ/cot θ = 1.

q.t: If cos 2θ = sin 4θ with both angles acute, find θ.
q.e: Complementary: 2θ + 4θ = 90°.

q.t: Find tan 7° tan 23° tan 60° tan 67° tan 83°.
q.e: tan 7° tan 83° = 1 and tan 23° tan 67° = 1, leaving tan 60° = √3.

q.t: Find sin² 1° + sin² 2° + … + sin² 89°.
q.e: Pairs (1°, 89°) … (44°, 46°) each give 1: that is 44, plus sin² 45° = 1/2.

q.t: If A + B = 90° and sin A = 3/5, find (tan A tan B + tan A cot B)/(sin A sec B) − sin² B/cos² A.
q.e: tan A tan B = 1, tan A cot B = tan² A, sin A sec B = 1 and sin B = cos A. So sec² A − 1 = tan² A = (3/4)².

q.t: Find cosec(65° + θ) − sec(25° − θ) − tan(55° − θ) + cot(35° + θ).
q.e: (65° + θ) + (25° − θ) = 90°, so the first two cancel; (55° − θ) + (35° + θ) = 90°, so the last two cancel.
